title: sorghum miliiforme
intro: Sorghum miliiforme, commonly known as milo, is a type of cereal crop belonging to the sorghum family and is native to Africa. It has been traditionally used in folk medicine for its potential health benefits, including lowering blood pressure, reducing inflammation, and aiding in digestion. The plant's bioactive constituents, such as flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, exhibit therapeutic actions such as antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties. These bioactive compounds are also thought to contribute to its potential therapeutic benefits, including its use as a natural remedy for wound healing, fever reduction, and as an anti-diabetic agent.
